title: Invasion Assay
description: Classify attached versus invaded parasites from pre- and post-permeabilization stains, derive field thresholds from controls, and report per-well efficiency with sensitivity and statistical QC.
objectives: Map the outside and total parasite stains without reversing the assay interpretation.
Derive and audit outside-stain thresholds using controls, bimodality, and sensitivity bounds.
Interpret per-field, per-well, and condition results with the well as the unit of replication.
prerequisite: Measure one row per segmented parasite in both a pre-permeabilization outside-stain channel and a post-permeabilization total-stain channel; include staining-control wells.

scenes.narration: Channels and Intensity maps channel one to the pre-permeabilization outside stain and channel zero to the post-permeabilization total stain. Attached parasites retain outside signal; invaded parasites lack it. Swapping these channels reverses the biological interpretation without causing a software error.

scenes.narration: During execution, the console reports threshold source and QC rather than showing only a final percentage. Inside is defined by absence of outside signal, so staining failure can only inflate invasion; sensitivity bounds make that direction of error visible.

scenes.narration: The real backend used three hundred sixty control parasites to set a threshold of twenty-two point eight, then scored one thousand four hundred forty experimental parasites across twelve wells and twenty-four fields. Vehicle wells average thirty-nine point seven percent invasion and inhibitor wells sixty-eight point nine percent; all wells pass QC. The Mann–Whitney test uses six wells per group and gives Holm-adjusted p zero point zero zero four zero six, while the much smaller pooled-parasite p-value is shown only to expose pseudoreplication inflation.
